dialog.body: Zoning and Inspections, this is Greg.

Hi, Greg, yes, hello. This is Celeste Duarte. I'm out on Gibbs Avenue, number 29, the Ocean Drive side. I want to put a little storage shed in the back yard and I got sent to three different people already, so I'm hoping you're the right one.
Sheds are us. Go ahead. What are you thinking, size-wise?

Well, that's my question, really. How big is too big? Because the one I looked at online is eight by ten, and then the guy at the hardware store said anything over a hundred square feet is a whole different thing, and then somebody else said no, that's the other town. I've called two numbers already today, and honestly I'm sick of being passed around.

Okay, I hear you. Generally there's a size under which a small shed is treated more simply, and above that you're into a full building permit. Eight by ten is eighty square feet, so you'd be on the smaller side. But the size is only part of it. Where it sits on the lot matters too, the setbacks from the property lines.

Setbacks. See, nobody mentioned that. My yard is sort of a funny shape, it narrows toward the back. My grandmother had a yard like that on Long Wharf, no, wait, it was, um, never mind, that's a whole story. Sorry. Setbacks.

No problem. So, how far from the back and side lines you can put it depends on your zoning district. If you give me the address I can look at what district you're in, and the permit office can tell you the distance.
It's 29 Gibbs Avenue. Twenty-nine.
Got it, give me a second here.

Sure. Oh, hang on, there's a truck in the road in front of me. Somebody's got a delivery truck stopped right in the middle blocking everybody, and there's a car behind it honking. Sorry, I'm in the car, I'm not at the house, I'm just parked near it. It's like every day with that.
That's all right. Take your time. I'm pulling up the parcel now.
They're moving. No, they're not. Okay, it doesn't matter. Go on.

Okay. So you'd be applying for a shed permit. It's a short form, a sketch of the lot showing where the shed goes with the distances to the lines, and the dimensions and height of the shed. Someone in the office reviews that against the district rules.
A sketch. Does it have to be, like, professional? Because I draw terribly.
No, it doesn't need to be professional. A clear hand drawing is usually fine as long as the measurements are labeled. Printing a copy of your survey and marking on it helps if you have one.

I have something from when we bought. I'll find it. It's in a folder somewhere. Now, do I need an inspection? Because if somebody has to come out and stand in my yard I need to know, I work and I can't just be home any old time.

Depends on the size and whether it has a foundation or electric. A simple shed sitting on blocks or a gravel pad with no electricity, often there's no big inspection. If you add power, that's a separate electrical permit and that does get inspected. The permit office will tell you when you apply whether anyone needs to come out.
No electric. I just want somewhere for the lawn mower and the rakes and the, um, the Christmas stuff. The bins are overflowing in the garage.
Then that's a pretty straightforward one. Do you know if the shed is coming prebuilt or if you're building it yourself?

Prebuilt, it comes on a truck. Which, ha, there's another truck. My whole day is trucks. Sorry. It comes in a kit, actually, you put it together. My brother-in-law says he'll do it but I don't trust him with a drill.
Either way the permit is about the finished structure. Just have the height ready. Taller sheds can run into limits too.
How tall is tall? Because this one is about eight feet at the peak.
Sorry, I mean, is eight feet okay?
Eight feet at the peak is typical for a small shed. I wouldn't expect a problem there, but put it on the form and they'll confirm.
Okay. And where do I get the form? Please don't say come in person, because I already drove around today.
You can pick it up here at City Hall, or it's on the city website under the permits page, and you can print it. If you can't print it, we can mail one.
The website, I'll try. If I can't find it I'll call back. Honestly, every number I called today said something different, so I'm glad you actually answered the thing.
Happy to. If you get stuck, ask for zoning and inspections and the setback question specifically, so they pull your district right away.
Setback, district. Let me write that down. Hold on. I'm writing on a receipt. Okay. Is there a number if I need you again? Or do I just call this one?
Same main line, ask for zoning and inspections. Or I can leave a note on the parcel that you called, so whoever picks up sees what we talked about.
Oh, yes, please do that. That would save me from telling the whole thing again. It's Celeste Duarte, and my cell is 401-555-0181.
Celeste Duarte, 401-555-0181, shed, 29 Gibbs Avenue, eight by ten, eight feet tall, no electric. Got it.
Perfect. That's exactly right. Okay, the truck finally moved, thank goodness. Thank you, Greg.
You're welcome. Have a good afternoon.
You too. Bye now.
